correctness.rationale: For strictly positive a_t,b_t, the two-mode similarity transform reduces M(d)F_t to N(x)B_t with x=1-d in [0,1], r_t=(a_t-b_t)/(a_t+b_t) in (-1,1). For k=2,3 exact trace and determinant formulas T_2=1+2s x+x²,D_2=q x²; T_3=1+s(x+x²)+x³,D_3=q x³ prove the endpoint domination by splitting at L=max(prod(1+r_t),prod(1-r_t)) above/below 1 and checking chi_x(1) or chi_x(L) nonnegative. The smaller eigenvalue is <=1, permitting Perron-root inference; k=1 follows from stochastic-column norm. Independent exact-rational multiplication reproduces k=4,d=24/25 matrix, trace 12320244/390625, determinant 36/78125 and characteristic value -1959399/1562500 at 63/2; endpoints give 30 and 63/2, so continuity forces an interior maximum. All unrestricted k<=3 inequalities are analytic, not extrapolations.
residual_risks: Does not claim optimizer uniqueness, extension to asymmetric mixing, stochasticity or more than two patches.

value.rationale: Determining the first temporal complexity at which a fixed intermediate dispersal strategy beats both complete retention and complete mixing is a natural mathematical cutoff for patch-growth optimization. Universal positivity over every sequence through three seasons plus a strict exact four-season witness establishes a structural boundary, not merely an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem distinguishes deterministic two-patch spectral fitness optimization from stochastic/evolutionary-policy objectives.
residual_risks: No inference to nonlinear ecology, stochastic growth or empirical species responses.

limitations: Strictly positive two-patch deterministic seasonal fitness; symmetric mixing; one constant d across phases.
